# session-hq

A shared, file-based headquarters for AI coding-agent sessions. One markdown status file per
domain, read at session start and written at session end, plus an ideas inbox, a decision log,
and a dispatch queue. The protocol is plain markdown; `scripts/hq.mjs` is a dependency-free Node
CLI; the Claude Code plugin is one adapter over it. Version 0.1.0, MIT.

## Who it is for

- [Problem statement](README.md): someone running several agent sessions who cannot see, across
  all of them, what is stalled, blocked, or untouched.
- [Why one session is not enough](docs/design.md): mixing and compaction push you to split by
  domain; splitting then costs you visibility, which is the problem this addresses.
- Not for a single session on a single project. The README says so.

## The three adapters

- [Claude Code hooks](hooks/hooks.json): the only fully automatic one. SessionStart and PreCompact
  inject, PostToolUse counts, Stop checks. Only this one can block a session from ending.
- [`hq.mjs wrap`](docs/adapters.md): prints the same context, runs any agent command with the
  terminal attached, propagates its exit code, checks on exit. No hooks required.
- [Instruction file](docs/adapters.md): three lines pasted into AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules
  or a system prompt. Convention, not enforcement — the docs label it as such.

## Commands

- `init`, `inject`, `remind`, `update-check`, `wrap` — set up and run a session
- `dispatch`, `done`, `ack`, `dispatches` — hand work to a domain and review the result
- `dashboard` — every domain on one screen; `--md` and `--html <file>`
- `inbox`, `decide`, `doctor`, `memory-lint`, `leak-check`
- Slash-command equivalents live in [commands/](commands/), one file each.

## Guarantees, and how to check them

- **No dependencies.** There is no `package.json` in the repo; nothing to install.
- **No network calls.** `grep -rE "fetch\(|https?://|node:https?|node:net" scripts/` returns
  nothing.
- **No telemetry.** Same grep; nothing is sent anywhere.
- **Reads four environment variables**, all its own: `HQ_ROOT`, `HQ_DOMAIN`, `HQ_MEMORY_DIR`,
  `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. Check with `grep -roE "env\.[A-Z_]+" scripts/`.
- **Writes only inside the HQ root** — `status-<domain>.md`, `ideas-inbox.md`, `decisions.md`,
  `dispatches.md`, `hq.config.json`, `.state/<session-id>.json` — plus the path you pass to
  `dashboard --html`. Check with `grep -rn "writeFileSync\|mkdirSync" scripts/`.
- **Runs one external process, and only on request:** the command after `--` in `wrap`
  ([scripts/lib/wrap.mjs](scripts/lib/wrap.mjs)); `leak-check` also shells out to `git ls-files`.
- **93 tests**, no network and no committed fixtures: `node --test`.
- [Security notes](docs/security.md): threat model, trust boundary, reporting.

## Non-goals, stated in the README

- No multi-account or usage-limit features. One account, many sessions.
- No API proxying, traffic-level model routing, or request interception.
- No automatic writing of status content — the tools remind, they never fabricate an entry.
- No claims about other tools' internals.

## Where to start reading

- [README.md](README.md) — problem, quick start for both adapter paths, configuration
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) — the argument, the tradeoffs, and what is deliberately absent

- [docs/case-studies.md](docs/case-studies.md) — three fictionalised failure modes
- [skills/hq-protocol/SKILL.md](skills/hq-protocol/SKILL.md) — what a good status entry contains

## How to verify the repo

- `node --test` — 93 tests
- `claude plugin validate . --strict` and `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json --strict`
- `node scripts/leak-check.mjs --denylist .github/leak-denylist.example.txt` — credential-shaped
  pattern scan over tracked files
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — CI matrix: ubuntu, macos, windows on Node 18 and 22
